reduction.witness: The required conclusion $g(t)\ge 0$ for every $t>0$ is not proved. The text would need to iterate (3) or (4) to obtain $f^n(t)=t+n g(t)>0$ for every integer $n\ge0$, which rules out $g(t)<0$. The displayed bound $g(x)>-x$ alone is insufficient.
reduction.load_bearing: Nonnegativity of every difference is part of the structural reduction and is later needed to classify the range of $g$.

upper_bound.quote:
Thus $V$ contains **at most one** positive number.  Consequently, either  

* (i) $g\equiv 0$ (constant), which gives $f(x)=x$, a solution; or  
* (ii) there is $c>0$ such that $V \subseteq \{0, c\}$ with both values attainable.
upper_bound.witness: The argument has shown only that two distinct positive values cannot occur; it has not written an argument excluding negative values of $g$. To cover all cases it must prove that $g(t)<0$ is impossible by iterating the orbit until $t+n g(t)\le0$. Without that step, the asserted dichotomy and all subsequent level-set arguments omit a case.
upper_bound.load_bearing: Sections 4–6 assume every point lies in $S_0\cup S_c$. Thus the claimed constancy of $g$ depends on the unwritten exclusion of negative differences.

parsed.notes: The stated answer and the QM–AM–GM verification are correct. The necessity proof has an unfilled negative-difference case before its range dichotomy.
